context:
Goal: after the CLAUDE.md moves you accepted today, a change to a moved rule is still flagged for review by the merge tool.
Problem (rule): your Oct 16 decision (claude-md-change-is-flagged, which files a change to gets flagged at merge) flags only CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md and the output-styles files, and says skills are not flagged; the moves put rules into skills and .claude/rules, so those rules lose the flag unless the list grows.
Based on (ruling): your Oct 16 decision, its file-list sentence and its "skills are not flagged" line.
Based on (read): merge/merge.py line 314 flags only the old list today; how often a flag in a skill file would be a false alarm is unmeasured.
Departs from: main flags only the old file list — the flag also covers each file the rule audit's list of rule-bearing files names, and the decision stops saying skills are never flagged.

options.gain: A moved rule still gets a reviewer round when it changes.
options.how: The merge tool flags a change to any file the rule audit lists as holding rules (lint/rule_audit.py, its RULE_FILES list), plus the old list; the decision is rewritten in place to say so. Other skills and agents stay unflagged.
options.label: Flag the rule-bearing files (Recommended)
options.lose: Any edit in those files, even a wording fix, owes a reviewer round.

options.how: Keep the Oct 16 decision as is and undo the lane's change to the merge tool.
options.label: Keep today's list
options.lose: A rule moved into a skill can change with no review flag.

reply: Filed: the merge tool flags every rule-bearing file the rule audit lists, plus the old list, and the Oct 16 decision is rewritten in place to say so. Lane global-claude-md-scope-audit builds it.
short: Moved rules keep their review flag
title: Rules moved out of CLAUDE.md keep their review flag at merge
why: Your own Oct 16 decision says skills are never flagged; only you can change it. Meanwhile the draft PR holds the merge tool change and leaves the decision untouched.
